newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Luka Koper slashes div, but 1996 net soars.
newsitem.headline: Luka Koper slashes div, but 1996 net soars.

text.p: Slovenian port operator Luka Koper reported on Wednesday a 53 percent surge in 1996 net profit but added it would slash its dividend to 100 tolars per share from 202.5 tolars in 1995.
The company said it was paring its dividend because the previous year's dividend had been paid from profits accumulated over the past three years.
Luka said net profit surged to 1.34 billion tolars from 877.4 million in 1995.
Sales at the tiny Alpine republic's only port reached 8.05 billion tolars, an 11 percent increase on 1995.
Luka, which debuted on Ljubljana's bourse in November, is 51 percent owned by the state, which has so far prevented international investors from taking a stake in the company.
On Wednesday, shares of Luka Koper firmed 1.07 percent or 19 tolars to close at 1,789 tolars on volume of 1,934 shares. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
